surprises.description: NWFL reported diluted EPS of $1.08, well above the preview’s $0.945 consensus estimate and above even the preview’s $1.02–$1.08 bull-case range except at its upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income reached a record $11.8 million, or $1.08 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $0.945”; the preview’s bull scenario projected “$1.02–1.08.”

surprises.description: Provision fell to just $100,000, far below the preview’s roughly $1.1 million estimate. The bankrupt borrower’s resolution reduced problem loans, and management said the remaining roughly $7 million exposure is real-estate secured with acceptable loan-to-values and no large loss anticipated, though the workout may take longer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Provision for credit losses fell sharply to $100,000 from $1.9 million in Q2, as the borrower bankruptcy resolution improved nonperforming loans”; “Approximately $7 million in remaining exposure” is secured with “acceptable loan-to-values and no large loss anticipated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Provision for credit losses” at “~$1.1M” and identified “the $22M nonperforming commercial credit” as the key credit issue.

surprises.description: Pre-provision net revenue was $15.4 million, above the roughly $13.9 million implied by the preview’s estimated $29.7 million revenue and $15.8 million expenses. It also rose 13% sequentially, indicating stronger pre-credit earnings than the preview’s model implied for the first clean post-integration quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pre-provision net revenue rose 53% year-over-year to $15.4 million, up 13% from $13.6 million in the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Total revenue” at “~$29.7M” and “Noninterest expense” at “~$15.8M”; those estimates imply about $13.9M of PPNR.

surprises.description: Net interest income reached $28 million, modestly above the preview’s $27.1 million estimate, although the preview already expected strong acquisition-driven growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest income grew 37% year-over-year to $28 million, driven by strong performance and the Presence Bank acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s model estimated “Net interest income” at “$27.1M.”

surprises.description: Reported NIM was 4.01%, above the preview’s expected roughly 3.85%–3.92% range. However, about 11 basis points came from a one-time borrower bankruptcy resolution, leaving the underlying margin roughly in line with the preview’s expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest margin expanded to 4.01%,” up 11 basis points sequentially, “though about $400,000 (roughly 11 bps) stemmed from the one-time borrower bankruptcy resolution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said reported NIM would “likely look fine (~3.85–3.92%)” and emphasized core NIM excluding one-time items.

surprises.description: The preview cited Q2 tangible book value of $22.96 per share, but Q3 tangible book value declined slightly to $22.35 as rising rates reduced the value of the available-for-sale portfolio. The preview did not forecast this decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tangible book value declined slightly to $22.35 per share due to lower other comprehensive income as rising rates reduced the market value of the available-for-sale portfolio.”

surprises.description: Management reported 41% year-over-year growth in the brokerage business after its transition to Cetera Wealth Services, a positive source of business growth the preview did not call out or forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Brokerage business grew 41% year-over-year following the transition to Cetera Wealth Services.”

surprises.description: Management supplied a go-forward tax-rate range of 21.5%–22%, which the preview did not anticipate or provide a comparison for.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “guiding to a go-forward tax rate of 21.5%-22%.”
